summary: Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford, later holding posts at Oxford, the London School of Economics, and Durham University.

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and completed his doctoral studies under Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, later serving on the faculty at the University of Sydney.
Michael J. Conway is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He serves as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and is attested as faculty at the Otani Academic Society in 2026.

Michael Coulson was an Indologist and linguist who completed his B.A. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. From 1966 to 1975, he served as Lecturer and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Edinburgh.

Michael Eido Luetchford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned an engineering degree at the University of Bradford. He studied traditionally under Gudo Wafu Nishijima from 1977 to 2007 and founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Fertig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Würzburg under Othmar Frank. He later worked as a Latin teacher at the University of Passau and served as Rector at Hans-Carossa-Gymnasium Landshut.
Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD and worked as an assistant at the University of Munich. He later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

Michael G. Morony is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA, becoming a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1974.

Michael Haberlandt was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Friedrich Müller and Georg Bühler. He held posts at the University of Vienna and served as Director of the Natural History Museum, Vienna.

Michael Hahn was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn and Marburg, including Marburg's chair of Indology and Tibetology.
Michael Harack is a scholar in religious studies and sinology who earned his Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).
Michael Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt is an Indologist and linguist who completed his BA and doctorate at the University of London. He held several posts at SOAS University of London, including Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean.

Michael I. Como is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and sinology who studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He holds an appointment at Columbia University, attested as Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies.

Michael J. Sweet was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry at Wisconsin-Madison.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who completed a Master of Arts degree at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned degrees at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, completing his doctorate under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner at the University of Vienna and University of Zurich. He held positions at the University of Zurich and the University of Münster.

Michael Jansen was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at RWTH Aachen University, Bonn, Rome, and Delhi. He served as Dean of Architecture at RWTH Aachen and founding rector of the German University of Technology in Oman.

Michael Jerryson was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer. He held academic posts at Eckerd College and Youngstown State University.
